case_title: V.P. Shrivastava v. Indian Explosives Ltd. & Ors.
statutory_provisions: IPC s.405, s.406, s.1208; Companies Act s.540, s.542
neutral_facts: The case involves a dispute between Indian Explosives Limited (IEL) and Fertilizer Corporation of India Limited (FCIL). FCIL entered into a tripartite agreement with IEL and Bharat Coking Coal Limited (BCCL) to supply ammonium nitrate to IEL in exchange for explosives. Due to financial difficulties and a breakdown of equipment, FCIL could not fulfill its obligations. FCIL was declared a sick company by the Board of Industrial and Financial Reconstruction (BIFR) and was directed to be wound up. IEL filed a criminal complaint against senior functionaries of FCIL, alleging cheating and criminal breach of trust under Sections 420, 406, and 1208 of the IPC, as well as Sections 540 and 542 of the Companies Act. The magistrate took cognizance of the complaint and issued summons against the accused. The accused filed a petition under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure to quash the summons, which was dismissed by the High Court. The Supreme Court allowed the appeals, set aside the High Court's order, and quashed the magistrate's order, finding no prima facie case against the accused.
